Pre-Surgical Diabetes Education Program Increased Preparedness for Diabetes Management after Total Pancreatectomy with Islet Autotransplantation.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Total pancreatectomy with islet autotransplantation (TPIAT) requires families to manage diabetes with insulin pumps and continuous glucose monitors postoperatively at our institution. Education occurs while the child is hospitalized after TPIAT, and one parent or caregiver receives all education. Diabetes self-management education and support (DSMES) must be effective, efficient, and completed with enough time for families to practice before discharge. We created a pre-TPIAT diabetes education program aimed at reducing subsequent inpatient education time and increasing the primary learner's preparedness for inpatient education.
METHODS: Thirty-three pediatric TPIAT recipients at Cincinnati Children's received presurgery education across three cycles of improvement. Data were extracted from clinical records and survey responses collected. Cohorts were well-balanced demographically (all P > 0.05, small effect sizes). Survey data, including paired knowledge assessments, were collected from Cohorts 2 and 3.
RESULTS: TPIAT recipients were predominantly White (87.9%), English speaking, non-Hispanic (97.0%), with balanced sex distribution (48.5% female). Mean age at surgery was 12.2 years. Parents were primary learners in 87.9% of cases. Presurgery education time showed highly statistically significant increases in Cohorts 2 and 3 compared with Cohort 1 (P = 0.0291 and P = 0.0007, respectively). Inpatient diabetes education showed a marginally significant decrease of 133 min from Cohort 1 to Cohort 2 (P = 0.0717) and directionally maintained in Cohort 3 (0.3285). Assessment results documented substantial knowledge acquisition from the intervention that was retained from pre- to postsurgery education. Learner confidence increased postintervention (P = 0.063), and overall satisfaction scores remained high except for stress/anxiety scores.
CONCLUSION: Changes in TPIAT diabetes education delivery effectively transferred some education to presurgery without compromising content, demonstrated by a statistically significant increase in presurgery education, knowledge scores that indicated retention of information, alongside numerically lower (nonsignificant) total inpatient education time after interventions.

title: Long-term clinical outcomes in females with precocious puberty treated with gonadotropin-releasing hormone analogues.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate long-term anthropometric, metabolic, reproductive, and bone mineral density (BMD) outcomes in girls with central precocious puberty (CPP) treated with Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone analogues (GnRHa).
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort with cross-sectional follow-up assessment, 82 of 265 eligible females (30.9%) with central precocious puberty or central hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis activation who had received GnRHa participated in long-term evaluation. Anthropometric outcomes, insulin sensitivity indices (HOMA-IR and QUICKI), hormonal profile, BMD, and reproductive outcomes including polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) were assessed. Analyses used available cases for each outcome; missing values were not imputed.
RESULTS: The mean age at final evaluation was 17.61 ± 4.3 years, and mean GnRHa treatment duration was 3.14 ± 1.9 years. Mean height at final follow-up was 159.85 ± 6.5 cm; the mean difference from baseline predicted adult height was 1.98 cm (95% CI, -0.37 to 4.34; P = 0.097). The distribution of BMI categories did not change significantly from baseline to final follow-up. Mean HOMA-IR and QUICKI were 3.76 ± 1.82 and 0.319 ± 0.025, respectively; among adults, 14/28 (50.0%) met each prespecified adult-derived threshold for reduced insulin sensitivity. PCOS was identified in 15/67 participants (22.4%). Mean lumbar and femoral BMD Z-scores were -0.25 ± 1.23 and -0.55 ± 1.03, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: Among participants who completed long-term follow-up, attained height was comparable at the group level with predicted adult and mid-parental height, and mean BMD Z-scores were within age- and sex-referenced ranges. PCOS and PCOS-related features were observed, while insulin sensitivity indices were associated with adiposity. Because only 30.9% of eligible patients participated and there was no untreated comparison group, these findings describe the evaluated cohort and should not be interpreted as causal effects of GnRHa treatment.

title: INSL3: an informative testis biomarker for assessing the HPG axis in men.
abstract: The male hypothalamo-pituitary-gonadal (HPG) axis is an integrated endocrine system linking hypothalamic GnRH secretion, pituitary gonadotropins (LH and FSH), Leydig cell steroidogenesis, Sertoli cell function, and spermatogenesis. While conventional parameters such as testosterone or LH may be subject to high biological variance due to their pulsatile mode of secretion and multiple stress-related or environmental influences, the Leydig-cell-secreted peptide insulin-like peptide 3 (INSL3) offers a robust and constitutive alternative reflecting Leydig cell number, differentiation status, and long-term functional capacity. This narrative review considers INSL3 across the male life course in relation to other components of the HPG axis, including in fetal development, minipuberty, pubertal development, and male aging. It shows how measuring INSL3 offers important granularity in understanding issues such as the effects of environmental endocrine disruption, childhood, and lifestyle influences on pubertal development as well as on adult Leydig cell capacity, hypogonadism, and age-related morbidity. The presented evidence suggests that INSL3 will prove to be a useful biomarker for the HPG axis in adult life, though the reference range in healthy adults is quite large for yet unknown reasons; associations with BMI as well as early childhood and adolescent influences are described. While INSL3 reflects the GnRH-LH-testosterone arm of the HPG axis and is normally not directly linked to the spermatogenic compartment and male fertility, some studies do suggest a supportive relationship which merits further research. Similarly, other functions of INSL3 in men also remain underexplored.

title: Comment on Redondo et al. BMI Normalization Is Associated With Lower Risk of Progression to Type 1 Diabetes, Primarily in Youth.

Type 1 Diabetes in the Youngest: From Distinct Needs to New Frontiers in Care.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) in very young children poses unique clinical and psychosocial challenges due to distinct physiological, developmental, and behavioural characteristics of this age group. Advances in diabetes technology, particularly hybrid closed-loop (HCL) systems, are transforming T1D management in young children by integrating continuous glucose monitoring with automated insulin delivery. Evidence from randomized controlled trials and real-world studies consistently demonstrates that HCL systems improve time in range (TIR), lower HbA1c, and reduce glycaemic variability, not only without increasing the risk of severe hypoglycaemia or diabetic ketoacidosis but actively decreasing their rates. Benefits are especially evident overnight, when glycaemic control is more stable, although daytime management remains more complex, due to unpredictable behaviours typical of preschoolers and marked circadian variability in insulin needs. Additional strategies, such as insulin dilution, may facilitate safer delivery of small doses, reducing the risk of nocturnal hypoglycaemia and improving time in range.
SUMMARY: Beyond metabolic outcomes, HCL systems substantially improve quality of life for both children and caregivers, reducing fear of hypoglycaemia, easing parental burden, and improving sleep and emotional well-being. Overall, current evidence supports HCL as a safe and effective therapeutic option for very young children with T1D, offering significant metabolic and psychosocial benefits, without completely eliminating the risk of hypoglycaemia. These findings highlight the need for further refinement of age-specific algorithms capable of addressing the unique physiological variability of this population.
KEY MESSAGES: This narrative review summarizes current evidence on the management of T1D in very young children, with particular focus on HCL systems and insulin dilution.

title: Familial 46,XX Ovotesticular Differences in Sex Development Associated With an NR5A1 p.Arg92Trp Variant.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: NR5A1 encodes steroidogenic factor 1 (SF-1), a key regulator of adrenal and gonadal development, steroidogenesis, AMH transcription, and the balance between pro-testicular and pro-ovarian pathways. The recurrent NR5A1 c.274C>T (p.Arg92Trp) variant is associated with SRY-negative 46,XX testicular and ovotesticular differences in sex development (DSD), but intrafamilial expression remains difficult to predict. Case Presentation We report a rare multigenerational familial presentation of SRY-negative 46,XX ovotesticular DSD associated with the heterozygous NR5A1 p.Arg92Trp variant. The proband was noted antenatally to have atypical genital development. Antenatal karyotyping confirmed a 46,XX, SRY-negative result. At birth, the proband had clitoromegaly, posterior labioscrotal fusion, a perineal urethral opening, absent vaginal opening, and palpable labioscrotal gonads. Testosterone, anti mullerian hormone (AMH), and inhibin B were elevated, consistent with functioning testicular tissue, while adrenal investigations were normal. Imaging and laparoscopy showed mixed Müllerian and Wolffian structures, and gonadal histology confirmed ovarian primordial follicles. The family history was notable for DSD in the mother's sister, who had undergone childhood genital surgery and gonadectomy, with histology showing intratubular germ cell neoplasia. She was the first family member found to carry the NR5A1 p.Arg92Trp variant, prompting targeted testing in the proband and her mother, both of whom were positive. The variant was subsequently identified in the maternal grandmother and in the proband's older 46,XX, SRY-negative brother, who was raised male and had typical male external genitalia with bilateral scrotal gonads; the mother's brother tested negative. The mother had previously been treated for a unilateral ovarian germ cell tumour. These findings demonstrate marked intrafamilial variability and highlight the importance of family-history-led genetic testing, tumour-risk assessment, and long-term multidisciplinary follow-up.
CONCLUSION: This family captures the striking phenotypic breadth of NR5A1 p.Arg92Trp within a single pedigree and illustrates the role of NR5A1 as a developmental regulator of gonadal fate and AMH-mediated ductal differentiation. It emphasises the need for cautious individualised management, tumour surveillance, long-term follow-up, genetic counselling, and psychological support.

title: Revisiting the β-Cell: The Key to the Type 2 Diabetes Puzzle: The 2025 Banting Medal for Scientific Achievement Award Lecture.
abstract: Major discoveries in the past have laid the foundation on which modern diabetes research has been built, and future findings can be anticipated. From this groundwork, we have pursued studies evaluating the role of β-cell function and β-cell mass in the pathogenesis of type 2 diabetes. In considering β-cell function, studies of β-cell responses to intravenous and oral glucose have highlighted the critical nature of interpreting these responses in the face of the prevailing insulin sensitivity, and not as isolated responses. The critical role of β-cell dysfunction in the pathogenesis of prediabetes and diabetes has become apparent. When prediabetes is present, β-cell function is reduced by 40%, while in recent-onset type 2 diabetes it is reduced by >80%. In youth with prediabetes and type 2 diabetes, β-cell function deteriorates at a faster rate than in adults, compatible with their disease being more aggressive. From clinical trials in both age groups, the progression of β-cell dysfunction over time is the basis for deteriorating glycemia, with none of the currently available glucose-lowering agents able to halt this inexorable decline. Reflecting on β-cell mass, this is clearly reduced in people with type 2 diabetes. One basis for this is islet amyloid, which is formed from the normal β-cell secretory peptide islet amyloid polypeptide (IAPP) (or amylin). The process of amyloid formation promotes oxidative stress, inflammation, and β-cell death, creating a destructive feed-forward that exacerbates disease progression. Experimental studies demonstrate that reducing amyloid formation reduces oxidative stress, inflammation, and the loss of β-cell mass. Ultimately, preserving β-cell function and mass is critical in striving to prevent and treat type 2 diabetes. Future tactics have to deviate from the current approaches if we are going to be successful in reducing the deleterious effects of a dysfunctional β-cell in type 2 diabetes.

title: Mixed Presentation of Hyperglycemic Hyperosmolar State and Diabetic Ketoacidosis in a Pediatric Patient: a Case Report and Literature Review.
abstract: The coexistence of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) and hyperglycemic hyperosmolar state (HHS), known as mixed hyperglycemic crisis, is a rare but potentially fatal metabolic emergency in pediatrics, and is frequently underrecognized because it is misclassified as isolated DKA. It carries a higher risk of complications than either entity alone, particularly in patients with complex comorbidities. We describe the case of a 16-year-old female with myelomeningocele, neurogenic bladder, obesity, and insulin resistance, who had self-discontinued treatment with metformin, atorvastatin, and allopurinol one year prior and presented with sudden neurological deterioration. Initial workup revealed extreme hyperglycemia (1,777 mg/dL), severe hyperosmolarity (431 mOsm/kg), decompensated metabolic acidosis (pH 7.13), and positive urine ketones (+++), consistent with a mixed DKA-HHS presentation. She subsequently developed septic shock of urinary origin, acute kidney injury, and acute pancreatitis (lipase 3,911 U/L). Despite intensive management guided by International Society for Pediatric and Adolescent Diabetes-ISPAD recommendations, she progressed to refractory shock and multiorgan failure, dying within 48 hours of admission. To the best of our knowledge, this represents one of the most extreme metabolic derangements reported in pediatric mixed hyperglycemic crisis. The convergence of extreme hyperosmolarity, concurrent sepsis, and structural comorbidities created a lethal risk phenotype in which sepsis, rather than the degree of metabolic derangement alone, appeared to determine the fatal outcome. Early recognition and an individualized therapeutic approach are essential to improve outcomes in vulnerable pediatric patients.

title: Diagnostic Performance of Urinary Clusterin for Early Detection of Diabetic Kidney Disease in Pediatric Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus: A Case-Control Analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Urinary Clusterin, a glycoprotein linked to oxidative stress and tubular injury, is being evaluated as a more sensitive biomarker for diabetic kidney disease (DKD). This study aims to assess the role of Clusterin in the early detection and prognostication of diabetic kidney disease in children with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM), addressing a critical gap in pediatric clinical data.
METHODS: This case-control study at Beni-Suef University compared 50 children with T1DM (duration ≥5 years) to 40 healthy controls. Assessments included Body Mass Index (BMI), glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), and lipid profiles. Urinary Clusterin was measured using Enzyme Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA). A Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was employed to determine the diagnostic performance of urinary Clusterin in detecting diabetic nephropathy.
RESULTS: Diabetic cases exhibited significantly higher levels of AST, cholesterol, triglycerides, and serum creatinine compared to the control group. The urinary profile revealed significantly elevated urinary creatinine, albumin, and albumin-to-creatinine ratios in cases, with urinary clusterin levels being significantly higher in children with diabetes (49.7 vs. 32.3 pg/mL, p<0.001) than in healthy controls. Within the case group, urinary clusterin significantly correlated with ALT, serum creatinine, and triglycerides, although no significant associations were found with age, BMI, or HbA1c. At a cutoff value of 37.6 pg/mL, urinary clusterin is a highly effective marker for early detection of diabetic nephropathy with an 80% sensitivity, and 90% specificity.
CONCLUSION: Urinary clusterin is a potential non-invasive biomarker for early diabetic nephropathy in children with T1DM, outperforming traditional measures and offering a promising tool for earlier screening and improved clinical management.

title: Sex, BMI, skeletal maturation, and height among children and adolescents in high-altitude Xizang: a cross-sectional study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Skeletal maturation influences the interpretation of childhood height, but its relationship with sex, body mass index (BMI), and attained height in children living at high altitude remains incompletely characterized. We examined concurrent associations among sex, BMI, bone-age deviation, and height relative to national reference values in children and adolescents living in Lhasa, Xizang.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 199 participants aged 3-16 years (101 girls and 98 boys). Bone-age deviation was defined as bone age minus chronological age. Height difference and BMI difference were calculated relative to age- and sex-specific national reference values. Multivariable linear regression incorporated centered chronological age and its quadratic term, ethnicity, BMI difference, and pubertal status, with HC3 heteroscedasticity-consistent standard errors. Statistical indirect associations through bone-age deviation were estimated using 5,000 participant-level bootstrap resamples.
RESULTS: Mean bone-age deviation was -0.64 ± 1.14 years. After adjustment, boys had a 0.65-year lower bone-age deviation than girls (95% CI, -0.96 to -0.33; P < 0.001). Each 1-kg/m² increase in BMI difference was associated with a 0.06-year increase in bone-age deviation (95% CI, 0.01 to 0.10; P = 0.010). Each 1-year increase in bone-age deviation was associated with a 2.76-cm greater height difference from the national reference (95% CI, 1.82 to 3.70; P < 0.001). The sex-related statistical indirect association through bone-age deviation was -1.78 cm (percentile 95% CI, -2.89 to -0.83; BCa 95% CI, -3.02 to -0.90). The corresponding direct association had confidence intervals spanning zero. Principal findings were generally retained in sensitivity analyses using grouped Tanner stages and after exclusion of influential or extreme observations.
CONCLUSION: In this Lhasa sample, boys showed greater skeletal maturation delay than girls, and skeletal maturity was strongly associated with current height relative to national references. Higher BMI relative to the corresponding reference was associated with more advanced skeletal maturation. These cross-sectional findings describe statistical associations and do not establish temporal mediation or an altitude-specific causal effect.

title: Retinoic acid signaling in growth plate development: receptor-specific effects, antagonist evidence, and pediatric translational considerations.
abstract: The growth plate is a spatially organized cartilage structure that drives longitudinal bone growth and is particularly vulnerable to nutritional imbalance, systemic disease, trauma, and drug exposure during childhood. Retinoic acid (RA), the bioactive metabolite of vitamin A, regulates transcription through retinoic acid receptors (RARα, RARβ, and RARγ). Its skeletal effects depend on concentration, developmental timing, tissue context, and receptor subtype. Physiologic RA homeostasis contributes to orderly chondrocyte maturation, whereas excessive or spatially inappropriate signaling can suppress proliferation, alter hypertrophic differentiation and extracellular matrix, and promote premature growth plate senescence or closure in experimental models. This narrative review integrates evidence on RA metabolism, RAR-dependent chondrocyte fate, and experimental RAR antagonists. Model-dependent antagonist effects include concurrent prevention of hedgehog inhibitor-associated closure and early post-injury attenuation of growth inhibition in juvenile mice; prevention during induction is not reversal of established physeal damage. Human zone-specific receptor biology remains insufficiently resolved, and apparently conflicting findings reflect differences in receptor pharmacology, tissue, developmental stage, timing, dose, and endpoint. Pediatric experience with systemic retinoids, including isotretinoin and the RARγ agonist palovarotene, underscores the developmental hazards of pathway modulation. Future studies should prioritize validated human growth plate models, receptor-subtype pharmacology, and longitudinal skeletal monitoring. RAR antagonism remains a preclinical, hypothesis-generating strategy requiring rigorous dose-window and long-term safety evaluation before pediatric clinical investigation.

title: Practice patterns in feminizing genitoplasty for disorders of sexual development: a national survey of pediatric surgical specialists.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Disorders of sex development (DSD) require a multidisciplinary approach to diagnosis and treatment. Feminizing genitoplasty (FG) is one of the main surgical interventions performed in DSD, although its timing and necessity remain controversial. This study aims to evaluate the perspectives of pediatric surgeons and pediatric urologists in Türkiye on FG.
METHODS: A structured online survey was administered to pediatric surgeons and pediatric urologists in Türkiye. The survey comprised demographic information, surgical experience, preferred surgical techniques, and follow-up practices. The responses were analyzed descriptively.
RESULTS: A total of 264 physicians' responses were collected. The majority of participants (57 %, n=151), possessing varying levels of experience and case numbers, reported performing FG procedures. While 73.7 % of this group conduct fewer than five FG surgeries annually, only 1.3 % perform more than 15. Preferences regarding surgical timing and techniques varied among physicians. Follow-up protocols differed considerably, with 49.3 % of respondents indicating the absence of long-term postoperative follow-up. The primary priorities in FG included the cosmetic appearance of the external genitalia (91.8 %), achieving a normal-sized clitoris and vagina (90.6 %), and ensuring functionality (94.1 %).
CONCLUSIONS: There is no consensus among pediatric surgeons and pediatric urologists in Türkiye on the timing and necessity of FG. The lack of standardized follow-up protocols and multidisciplinary decision-making mechanisms remains a significant issue. Further research with larger cohorts and long-term outcome assessments is necessary to establish clearer guidelines.

title: Progesterone levels on hCG trigger day and neonatal outcomes in fresh embryo transfers: a retrospective threshold analysis of GnRH antagonist versus agonist long protocols.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Elevated progesterone levels on the day of human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) trigger are known to adversely affect pregnancy outcomes in fresh embryo transfer (fET) cycles, but their impact on neonatal outcomes remains poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate the association between progesterone levels on hCG trigger day and neonatal outcomes, and to explore the progesterone threshold, so as to provide reference for clinical decision-making.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 2, 201 patients who achieved singleton live births following fET between April 1, 2021 and December 31, 2024. All patients were ≤ 42 years of age and underwent either a GnRH antagonist protocol or an agonist long protocol. A multivariable regression analysis was performed to detect the relationship between progesterone level and neonatal outcomes. Smooth curve fitting and threshold effect analysis were used to evaluate the cutoff value of progesterone level.
RESULTS: In the overall population, higher progesterone levels were significantly associated with increased risks of preterm delivery (PTD) (adjusted OR: 1.89, 95% CI: 1.03 to 3.47, P = 0.0399) and low birthweight (LBW) (adjusted OR: 2.67, 95% CI: 1.14 to 6.24, P = 0.0231). These associations were observed only in the GnRH antagonist protocol, particularly with progesterone ≥ 1.0 ng/mL significantly elevating the risks of PTD (adjusted OR: 4.54, 95% CI: 2.16 to 9.56, P = 0.0021) and LBW (adjusted OR: 4.16, 95% CI: 1.15 to 15.07, P = 0.0378). Threshold analysis further identified progesterone > 0.90 ng/mL as the inflection point for PTD (adjusted OR: 6.60, 95% CI: 2.52 to 14.56, P = 0.0131) and progesterone > 0.98 ng/mL for LBW (adjusted OR: 7.50, 95% CI: 3.71 to 15.87, P = 0.0038) in antagonist cycles. No such associations were found in the GnRH agonist long protocol.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that in GnRH antagonist cycles, a serum progesterone level exceeding 0.90 ng/mL on hCG trigger day may serve as an independent predictor of an increased risk of PTD in singletons born after fET. These results highlight the need for enhanced perinatal surveillance in this population, and call for further validation in larger prospective multicenter studies.

title: The relationship between symptoms of adenomyosis and current ultrasonographic diagnostic criteria.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Adenomyosis is a uterine disorder defined by presence of endometrial glands and stroma within the myometrium with surrounding myometrial hyperplasia. Research has shown that ultrasound (US) can play a key role in early adenomyosis diagnosis and treatment. The Morphological Uterus Sonographic Assessment (MUSA) recently published standardized criteria for ultrasonographic diagnosis of adenomyosis, but the relationship between these criteria and clinical symptoms, has yet to be clinically validated.
OBJECTIVES: To assess the prevalence of MUSA ultrasound criteria of adenomyosis and relationship between rates of ultrasound features and clinical symptoms of adenomyosis.
METHODS: This is an analytical cross-sectional study of patients aged 18-52 receiving a transvaginal ultrasound for any indication at a single outpatient imaging center. Patients were excluded if they had a hysterectomy and/or bilateral oophorectomy, were in menopause, or had active gynecologic malignancy. Patients completed a survey to assess for infertility or fertility-related healthcare use, heavy menstrual bleeding, and pelvic pain. Ultrasound images were assessed by a radiologist using MUSA criteria to evaluate for adenomyosis. Multivariate analyses assessed association between MUSA features and patient-reported symptoms.
RESULTS: Of 271 recruited participants, 11.4% had at least one direct feature of adenomyosis, 57.6% had no direct features but at least one indirect feature, and 31.0% had no features. After controlling for potential confounders in multivariable analysis, patients with direct features resulted in 5.955-point higher heavy bleeding scores compared to those with no features (95% CI 1.970-9.939, p=0.004). When controlling for covariates, the association between indirect features and adenomyosis symptoms were not significant. Subjects with middle myometrium invasion reported increased rates of infertility (p=0.006), whereas subjects with outer myometrial involvement reported significantly higher heavy bleeding (p=0.002).
CONCLUSIONS: Per MUSA criteria, 1 in 10 participants displayed ultrasonographic findings strongly suggestive of presence of adenomyosis. Patients with direct features were more likely to experience heavy menstrual bleeding. Layer of uterine involvement were found to have greater association with infertility and pelvic pain than any one MUSA feature.

title: Fertility preservation counselling in women with cancer: knowledge, preferences, and unmet needs from a cross-sectional survey.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fertility preservation (FP) is a critical survivorship issue for young women with cancer, yet gaps persist between guidelines and clinical practice. This study assesses knowledge, attitudes, and unmet needs among women referred for specialist counseling.
METHODS: An observational cross-sectional survey was conducted (November 2022 - June 2026) among women referred to a single tertiary oncofertility center in Rome. A Delphi-informed online questionnaire was completed before the clinical visit. Descriptive statistics and exploratory multivariable logistic regression examined post-diagnosis intention.
RESULTS: Among 284 women invited to participate, 260 completed the survey (response rate, 91.5%); 240 patients with a confirmed cancer diagnosis were included in the final analysis (median age, 32 years). Overall, 69.6% were interested in FP, and 94.2% recognized that gonadotoxic treatments could impair fertility. While 89.6% had heard of FP, only half received this information from healthcare professionals, and 24.2% knew of no specific options. Over half reported concerns regarding treatment delay, safety, effectiveness, and cost. Before diagnosis, 73.7% planned to have children; post-diagnosis, positive intention remained common, while those previously without intentions shifted toward uncertainty. In the 188-case model, pre-diagnosis intention showed the strongest association (OR 11.64, 95% CI 4.45-30.48). Given limited model performance (pseudo-R²=0.19), estimates warrant caution.
CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center referred cohort, informational gaps and uncertainty remained despite high awareness. Findings confirm and contextualize prior evidence in an Italian tertiary setting and may inform similar referral pathways, but require validation in broader populations.

title: First-morning urinary luteinizing hormone and bone age decomposition for diagnosis of central precocious puberty in girls: a two-step prediction model study.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The diagnosis of central precocious puberty (CPP) in girls relies on the invasive gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) stimulation test. Urinary luteinizing hormone (LH) is a noninvasive candidate biomarker, but evidence from Chinese populations and its integration into multivariable prediction frameworks remain limited. We evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of first-morning urinary LH for CPP, established sex- and pubertal stage-specific reference intervals, and developed a two-step prediction model based on a bone age decomposition.
METHODS: In this single-center retrospective diagnostic accuracy study, we enrolled 808 children: 295 girls with early breast development (146 CPP, 149 non-CPP), 271 healthy girls, and 242 healthy boys (reference intervals only). First-morning urine was assayed for LH, follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), and creatinine. Diagnostic performance was evaluated primarily in the 295 symptomatic girls, with an extended analysis in 566 girls including healthy controls; multivariable logistic regression decomposed bone age into chronological age (CA) and the BA-CA difference as separate predictors.
RESULTS: Urinary LH showed moderate accuracy for CPP in the primary symptomatic cohort (AUC 0.692, 95% CI 0.630-0.752), peaking in girls aged 7-8 years (AUC 0.708, 95% CI 0.621-0.785); the extended cohort gave similar results (AUC 0.712; secondary, spectrum-extended estimate). The LH-to-creatinine ratio offered no improvement. Basal serum LH was the superior single marker (AUC 0.868 vs 0.692, P < 0.001). The noninvasive Model 1 (CA + BA-CA + urinary LH + breast Tanner stage + uterine length) achieved a C-statistic of 0.853 (sensitivity 73.3%, specificity 83.2%), with CA, BA-CA, and urinary LH as independent predictors. Adding basal serum LH and FSH (Model 2) improved the C-statistic to 0.909; urinary LH retained independent significance (aOR 1.280, P = 0.024), whereas basal FSH was inversely associated with CPP. Bootstrap-corrected C-statistics were 0.838 (Model 1) and 0.893 (Model 2). Pubertal-onset cutoffs were >1.02 mIU/mL in girls and >0.95 mIU/mL in boys.
CONCLUSIONS: Decomposing bone age into CA and BA-CA enables tiered CPP risk stratification: the noninvasive model supports initial screening without blood sampling, and the complete model refines risk once serum gonadotropins become available. Urinary LH is a clinically useful component of tiered diagnostic algorithms for CPP.

title: Disease duration and C-peptide at onset are key determinants of long-term residual β-cell function in children with type 1 diabetes.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Residual β-cell function (RBCF) may persist in a subset of children with long-standing type 1 diabetes (T1D), offering metabolic benefits. We aimed to evaluate factors that determine the long-term persistence of RBCF.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective study from July 2024 to December 2025 to assess RBCF in children with long-standing (≥7 years) T1D. Stimulated C-peptide (SCP) was measured 90 min after the mixed-meal tolerance test. Patients were grouped into RBCF-preserved (SCP ≥0.01 nmol/L) or RBCF-depleted (SCP <0.01 nmol/L). RBCF determinants, such as age, sex, ketoacidosis at onset, serum C-peptide concentration at diagnosis, number of pancreatic autoantibodies at diagnosis, glycemic control, and disease duration, were compared between the two groups.
RESULTS: Seventy-two children (mean age 15.4 ± 3.3 years, 54 % boys) with a mean T1D duration of 9.8 ± 2.1 years were studied. RBCF was preserved in 30.6 % (22/72) of children. Shorter disease duration (median 8.8 vs. 9.7 years, p=0.027) and higher C-peptide at onset (0.17 vs. 0.04 nmol/L, p<0.001) strongly predicted preservation. Older age at T1D onset (7.3 vs. 4.9 years) showed a trend toward better-preserved RBCF, but the association did not attain statistical significance (p=0.11). Ketoacidosis at onset, the number of autoantibodies, and glycemic control did not affect RBCF persistence.
CONCLUSIONS: RBCF persists in about one-third of children with long-standing T1D, suggesting that endogenous insulin production does not vanish completely after diagnosis. Higher C-peptide levels at clinical onset strongly predicted long-term RBCF-preservation, suggesting that patients with a larger initial β-cell reserve are better poised for long-term endogenous insulin synthesis.

title: Long-term Cost-Effectiveness of an Automated Insulin Delivery System Versus Multiple Daily Injections of Insulin Plus Continuous Glucose Monitoring in Children and Adults With Type 1 Diabetes in Hong Kong.
abstract:
AIM: The MiniMed 780G (MM780G) automated insulin delivery (AID) system has been shown to improve glycemic control in people with type 1 diabetes (T1D). The aim was to determine the long-term cost-effectiveness of the MM780G versus multiple daily injections of insulin plus continuous glucose monitoring (MDI+CGM) in people with T1D in Hong Kong.
METHODS: The analysis was performed using the IQVIA Core Diabetes Model. The primary analysis was performed in adults with HbA1c ≥8%, from a payer perspective over a time horizon of 60 years and annual discount rate of 3%. Clinical input data were sourced from a clinical trial, wherein HbA1c reductions from baseline (9.04%) of 1.54% and 0.2% were assumed for MM780G and MDI+CGM, respectively. A secondary analysis was performed for a cohort of children/adolescents starting treatment at <18 years.
RESULTS: In the adult base case analysis, the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) for MM780G versus MDI+CGM was HKD 348 927 (USD 44 759) per quality-adjusted life year (QALY) gained. In the pediatric analysis, the ICER for MM780G versus MDI+CGM was HKD 300 466 (USD 38 543) per QALY. The use of MM780G was predicted to result in reductions in the incidence of diabetes-related complications in both analyses.
CONCLUSION: Over a long-term time horizon, the use of MM780G was projected to improve clinical outcomes versus MDI+CGM. The MM780G was found to be cost-effective versus MDI+CGM in adults with T1D in Hong Kong who are not achieving glycemic targets; benefits were more pronounced in pediatric users, underscoring the value of initiating AID therapy at a younger age.

title: Congenital generalized lipodystrophy type 1 presenting with prominent immaturebrown adipose tissue in a preterm neonate: a case report.
abstract: Congenital generalized lipodystrophies (CGL) are genetic disorders characterized by generalized lipoatrophy and severe metabolic complications. Neonatal diagnosis remains uncommon because the typical phenotype may not yet be fully established. We report a preterm female neonate presenting with rapidly progressive bilateral cervical, axillary, and inguinal masses. Imaging and histopathological examination identified prominent immature brown adipose tissue. Severe hypertriglyceridemia prompted suspicion of CGL, which was subsequently confirmed by identification of a homozygous pathogenic AGPAT2 variant. During follow-up, generalized lipoatrophy, insulin resistance, and hepatic steatosis progressively developed, whereas the brown adipose tissue deposits completely regressed by 8 months of age. Nutritional management with a medium-chain triglyceride-enriched formula resulted in marked metabolic improvement. This case highlights that prominent immature brown adipose tissue associated with severe neonatal hypertriglyceridemia may represent an early manifestation of CGL1 and should prompt early genetic investigation.

title: Incidence of Pediatric Hyperglycemic Hyperosmolar State: A Prospective National Surveillance Study.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Hyperglycemic hyperosmolar state (HHS) is a severe diabetic emergency, typically seen in adults with type 2 diabetes, but with high morbidity described in the limited pediatric cases available in the literature. Existing estimates of pediatric HHS incidence are primarily derived from administrative datasets and may be affected by diagnostic misclassification. We sought to determine the minimum incidence, clinical characteristics, management, and outcomes of pediatric HHS.
METHODS: Approximately 2,700 pediatricians and pediatric subspecialists were surveyed monthly from June 2023 through May 2025 to identify cases of pediatric HHS, via the Canadian Paediatric Surveillance Program. Cases were adjudicated using predefined biochemical criteria, including severe hyperglycemia, elevated serum osmolality (>320 mOsm/kg), and absence of significant acidosis. Detailed clinical data were collected for confirmed cases.
RESULTS: Twenty-four cases were reported during the 24-month surveillance period. Following case adjudication, seven cases met diagnostic criteria for HHS, corresponding to a minimum annual incidence of 0.059 cases per 100,000 child-years (95% CI 0.024-0.122). Median age at presentation was 14.8 years, and all cases occurred in individuals with newly diagnosed or previously unrecognized diabetes. Common precipitating factors included infection, trauma, and surgery. Most patients required intensive care admission, with a median hospital stay of six days. Frequent complications included acute kidney injury and hypokalemia, and one patient required intervention for suspected cerebral injury, although no deaths were reported. Half of initially reported cases were subsequently reclassified as hyperosmolar diabetic ketoacidosis, highlighting challenges in the recognition and classification of pediatric hyperglycemic emergencies.
CONCLUSION: National surveillance in Canada identified lower incidence of HHS, indicating that prior estimates based on administrative data likely overstate rates due to misclassification of hyperglycemic emergencies.

title: FSH-secreting pituitary adenomas presenting with spontaneous ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome in children and adolescents: two cases, a literature review, and long-term follow-up.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Functioning FSH-secreting pituitary adenomas (FSHomas) are exceedingly rare in children; only nine pediatric patients, seven girls and two boys, have been reported previously. In girls, they commonly present with spontaneous ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (sOHSS). The clinical presentation, management, and long-term outcomes of these tumors remain incompletely characterized.
CASE PRESENTATION: We report two girls aged 10.1 and 16 years with prolonged menstrual bleeding and bilateral multicystic ovarian enlargement due to FSHoma-associated sOHSS. Both demonstrated markedly elevated estradiol, suppressed LH, and nonsuppressed (inappropriately normal) FSH, with pituitary adenomas of 14 × 11 × 13 mm and 9 × 9 mm on MRI; immunohistochemistry was FSHβ-positive in both. Case 1 underwent transsphenoidal adenectomy after medical treatment with letrozole and cabergoline; despite residual tumor tissue, she remained stable over 10 years of follow-up. Case 2 underwent transsphenoidal resection but developed recurrent hyperestrogenism and ovarian enlargement 5 years later despite radiological stability of the residual adenoma, and subsequently required emergency surgery for ovarian torsion (excision of the left ovary, right ovarian cystectomy). All 11 pediatric patients, including the present two, were compared for presentation, treatment, and long-term outcome.
CONCLUSIONS: These cases provide 10 and 9 years of follow-up after diagnosis. Biochemical recurrence may occur independently of radiological tumor progression, and persistent ovarian stimulation from residual adenoma tissue may cause irreversible complications, including ovarian torsion. Long-term multidisciplinary surveillance with serial hormonal assessment, pelvic imaging, and pituitary MRI is essential, and early pituitary-directed intervention may prevent unnecessary gynecological surgery.

title: Apparent mineralocorticoid excess mimicking Bartter syndrome in infancy.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Apparent mineralocorticoid excess (AME) syndrome is a rare monogenic disorder caused by loss-of-function variants in the HSD11B2 gene encoding 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2 (11β-HSD2). Deficient enzyme activity results in cortisol-mediated activation of the mineralocorticoid receptor, leading to low-renin hypertension. Because affected infants frequently present with polyuria and hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis, AME syndrome is often misdiagnosed as Bartter syndrome, resulting in significant diagnostic delay.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 13-month-old girl presented with polyuria, hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis, hypercalciuria, and failure to thrive and was initially managed as Bartter syndrome. During follow-up, persistent hypertension accompanied by markedly suppressed plasma renin activity and aldosterone levels prompted evaluation for monogenic hypertension. Urinary steroid analysis demonstrated a markedly reduced cortisone-to-cortisol ratio (0.02), consistent with 11β-HSD2 deficiency. Next-generation sequencing of the HSD11B2 gene identified a homozygous likely pathogenic splice-site variant, c.665-1G>A, confirming the diagnosis of AME syndrome. Treatment with spironolactone, amlodipine, potassium supplementation, and dietary salt restriction achieved blood pressure control and improved electrolyte abnormalities.
CONCLUSIONS: AME syndrome should be included in the differential diagnosis of infants presenting with hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis and polyuria, particularly when hypertension is detected. Systematic blood pressure assessment is essential in this clinical context, as early recognition of this monogenic disorder may prevent long-term cardiovascular and renal complications.

title: The Variable Presentation and Diagnostic Pitfalls of Autonomous Thyroid Nodules in Pediatrics: A Single-Center Case Series.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Thyroid nodules are less common and more likely to be malignant in children than in adults. Data on pediatric autonomous thyroid nodules (ATN) are scarce.
METHODS: Retrospective descriptive study. Twelve-year single-center case series of 12 patients (8 females) diagnosed with ATN at median age 15.7 years (3.6-17.3). A thirteenth patient with papillary thyroid carcinoma and hyperthyroidism was reported and described in the study but their data were not included in the descriptive statistics due to uncertainty regarding the autonomous nature of their nodule.
RESULTS: Over half the patients presented with a goiter and/or palpable nodule (72.7%). Symptoms of hyperthyroidism were present in 75%. Laboratory findings included suppressed serum TSH (100%). Free T4 was either normal (92.7%) or elevated (8.3%) with elevated total T3 (33.3%). Positive thyroperoxidase or thyroglobulin auto-antibodies were reported in three (25%) and one (8.3%) patients respectively. Two patients (16.7%) had TSH receptor antibodies at baseline. On ultrasound, thyroid nodule sizes were 2-4 cm (75%) or above 4 cm (25%). TIRADS scores were: 1 (8.3%), 2 (33.3%), 3 (8.3%), 4 (25%) or 5 (25%). Findings typical of ATN were detected in 10 of 11 patients (90.9%) on scintigraphy. Cytopathology was available on 8 nodules from 5 patients. Bethesda classifications were: II (n=2), III (n=3), IV (n=1), and V (n=1). Molecular analysis showed activating TSH receptor mutation in three of five tested patients. Ten patients completed surgery: total thyroidectomy (n=1) or lobectomy (n=9). Pathology was consistent with benign nodules in 9 cases. In one, the ATN was benign, but pathology detected incidental thyroid microcarcinoma in the same lobe.
CONCLUSIONS: The presentation of children with ATN is highly variable. Clinical signs of hyperthyroidism may not be present initially and the interpretation of laboratory and imaging data could be complicated by confounding factors . Multicenter studies are needed to establish the frequency of malignancy in pediatric ATN and better understand its pathophysiology.

title: SEMAGLUTIDE TREATMENT IN TWO VERY YOUNG CHILDREN WITH SEVERE EARLY-ONSET OBESITY.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Monogenic obesity comprises a group of rare genetic disorders characterized by severe early-onset obesity and hyperphagia. Pharmacological treatment options for severe early-onset obesity remain limited, particularly in young children.
CASE PRESENTATION: We report two children younger than 6 years of age with severe early-onset obesity, including one with genetically confirmed monogenic obesity, who showed reductions in BMI-SDS during semaglutide treatment. Case-1: A 4.5-year-old girl with a homozygous ADCY3 (c.1102G>A) variant presented with severe obesity, hyperphagia, hypertension, hepatosteatosis and Blount's disease. Baseline BMI was 48.0 kg/m2 (+5.5 SDS). Semaglutide was initiated at 0.125 mg/week and titrated to 1.5 mg/week. After 18 months, BMI-SDS decreased from +5.5 to +4.1 (-25.5%), accompanied by improved in hyperphagia and resolution of left ventricular hypertrophy. No significant adverse effects were observed, and linear growth remained age appropriate. Case-2: A 3.3-year-old boy with hyperphagia, severe obesity and dyslipidaemia was diagnosed with Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY). Clinical Exome Sequencing identified no causative variant for obesity. Baseline BMI was 32.6 kg/m2 (+5.7 SDS). Semaglutide was initiated at 0.0625 mg/week and gradually titrated to 2.0 mg/week. After 21 months, BMI-SDS decreased from +5.7 to +4.4 (-22%). Treatment was generally well tolerated, with normal linear growth.
CONCLUSION: This two cases describe reductions BMI-SDS during semaglutide treatment in very young children with severe early-onset obesity, including one child with genetically confirmed ADCY3-related monogenic obesity. These findings suggest a potential clinical benefit of semaglutide in this young population, warranting evaluation in larger studies.

title: Isolated increased free-triiodothyronine in medication-naïve children and adolescents with ADHD: a retrospective observational study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thyroid hormones, free triiodothyronine (free-T3) in particular, are crucial for fetal development and child growth and may influence neurodevelopmental disorders including Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) in children and adolescents. Yet data are scarce and inconsistent, often relying on adult rather than pediatric reference intervals or on incomplete thyroid panels, and the value of free-T3 as a biomarker across development remains unclear.
METHODS: In this retrospective observational study, we characterized thyroid function in medication-naïve patients aged 6 to 17 years with ADHD, using community laboratory results collected between March 2004 and December 2022 in a university pediatric department. Thyroid testing was prescribed prior to methylphenidate initiation. We determined the percentage of patients with free-T3, free-T4, and TSH levels below, within, or above age- and sex-adjusted reference intervals. In the largest immunoassay subgroup (ADVIA Centaur; n = 404), individual free-T3 values were converted to z-scores using published pediatric normative data. A longitudinal ancillary analysis assessed temporal stability in patients with repeat measurements. No non-ADHD comparison group was available.
RESULTS: Among 715 medication-naïve patients with ADHD (570 boys, 145 girls) with normal TSH, approximately one-third presented with isolated increased free-T3 concentrations (2IfT3 profile) - 33.68% of boys, 27.59% of girls - the most frequent thyroid anomaly observed. In the ADVIA Centaur subgroup, free-T3 z-scores were higher than the pediatric norms across all age groups, with the largest deviation in boys aged 11-14 years. Among 57 patients with repeat testing (median interval 2.57 years), instability was marked: 53.57% of those initially showing 2IfT3 normalized, while 50% of those initially normal developed 2IfT3.
CONCLUSION: Isolated increased free-T3 is frequent in medication-naïve pediatric ADHD and most pronounced in boys aged 11-14 years, but its marked temporal instability precludes its use as a stable biomarker. In the absence of a concurrent non-ADHD comparison group, these findings describe the frequency of this biochemical profile within an ADHD cohort rather than establishing an association with ADHD itself. The 2IfT3 profile may reflect a developmentally and state-dependent neuroendocrine pattern, and warrants prospective study incorporating direct pubertal staging, standardized assay methodology, and appropriate controls.

title: Case Report: Sustained pubertal suppression for 68 months with a single histrelin acetate implant in central precocious puberty.
abstract: The subcutaneous histrelin acetate implant is FDA-approved for 12 months of continuous gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) agonist therapy in central precocious puberty (CPP). Published data demonstrated sustained suppression with a single implant for up to approximately 24 months; however, efficacy beyond this duration has not been reported. A 7 years 5 month old female patient presented with bilateral Tanner 2 breast development, a bone age of 10 years, and laboratory findings consistent with early central activation. Treatment was delayed 11 months due to disruptions in care during the COVID-19 pandemic, and a histrelin implant was placed at age 8 years 5 months. The patient was lost to follow-up and returned at nearly 14 years of age, approximately 68 months after the implant placement, with primary amenorrhea and pubertal arrest. Laboratory evaluation before implant removal showed suppressed but detectable gonadotropins with a prepubertal estradiol, consistent with sustained partial suppression of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal (HPG) axis sufficient to arrest pubertal progression. Her predicted adult height (PAH) of 167.6 cm (66 inches) approximated her mid-parental height (MPH) of 166.4 cm (65.5 inches). This case demonstrates that a single histrelin acetate implant may maintain clinically meaningful pubertal suppression for at least 68 months. These findings support broader investigations into the pharmacokinetics of extended implant use, given implications for reducing surgical burden and healthcare costs in CPP management.

title: Metabolic-inflammatory heterogeneity in PCOS assisted reproduction: a compartmental susceptibility model.
abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a heterogeneous endocrine-metabolic disorder rather than a uniform reproductive diagnosis. Women entering assisted reproductive technology (ART) differ in adiposity, insulin sensitivity, lipid metabolism, androgen excess, inflammatory activity, and oxidative stress, but these systemic traits do not map uniformly onto the follicular or endometrial compartments. We propose a testable compartmental susceptibility model in which systemic metabolic-inflammatory burden acts as a background exposure and clinically relevant effects emerge when stage-specific follicular-oocyte or endometrial-maternal vulnerability is also present. Evidence was interpreted with a pragmatic hierarchy that separates guideline/RCT evidence, registry and externally validated prognostic evidence, adjusted observational associations, mechanistic discovery studies, and protocol-only evidence. Current data support metabolic assessment, prevention of excessive ovarian response, and maternal risk surveillance, but they do not validate a metabolic-inflammatory subtype for selecting stimulation, trigger, frozen-embryo-transfer preparation, immune adjuncts, or other phenotype-specific treatment. Local immune, extracellular-vesicle, and multi-omics signals remain discovery tools rather than clinical tests. Precision ART in PCOS will require paired systemic-local phenotyping, external validation, and prospective phenotype-by-treatment interaction studies using cumulative live birth and maternal-neonatal safety as primary endpoints.

title: Paternally Inherited DIO3 Loss and Infantile-Onset Central Hypothyroidism: Human Evidence for a Novel Mechanism of Hypothalamic-Pituitary-Thyroid Axis Dysregulation.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: DIO3 encodes type 3 iodothyronine deiodinase, the major thyroid hormone-inactivating enzyme, and is an imprinted gene with preferential paternal-allele expression demonstrated in human neonatal skin. Dio3-deficient mice develop neonatal thyrotoxicosis followed by central hypothyroidism, but human evidence has been lacking.
PATIENT FINDINGS: On newborn screening, thyrotropin (TSH) and free thyroxine (fT4) did not meet repeat-testing criteria, while T-cell lymphopenia was detected neonatally. From 5 months onward, fT4 progressively declined without compensatory TSH elevation. Chromosomal microarray identified a derivative chromosome 14 with a 14q32.31-q32.33 deletion encompassing DIO3 and TRAF3. The deletion originated from a paternal balanced 4p/14q translocation.
SUMMARY: In this patient, delayed-onset central hypothyroidism was most consistent with paternal DIO3 loss, whereas the accompanying T-cell lymphopenia was consistent with TRAF3 haploinsufficiency.
CONCLUSIONS: This case provides the first human evidence linking paternal DIO3 loss to delayed-onset central hypothyroidism, supporting a novel developmental mechanism that may alter hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid axis programming.

journal.title: Thyroid : official journal of the American Thyroid Association

title: Technology use in youth with type 1 diabetes and language of care other than English.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Our primary aim was to describe continuous glucose monitor (CGM) and insulin pump use in youth with T1D with a preferred language of care other than English (LOE) and examine associations between diabetes technology use and hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) in this population.
METHODS: We assessed baseline technology use for youth with LOE and T1D seen in diabetes clinics at a single center between February 2022 and February 2023. A two-sample t-test was used to compare HbA1c values between groups. A linear regression model was used to examine differences in HbA1c between the 3-level technology groups with Tukey-adjusted pairwise comparisons.
RESULTS: Ninety-four youth with T1D and LOE with complete data on technology use were included in analysis. At baseline 66 % were using diabetes technology with 42 (45 %) using CGM only, 1 (1 %) using insulin pump only, 19 (20 %) using both insulin pump and CGM, and 32 (34 %) not using any technology. HbA1c was significantly lower in the technology use group (Mean=9.1 %, SD=2.4) compared to the non-technology use group (Mean=10.5 %, SD=2.2) (p=0.01).
CONCLUSIONS: Despite advances in technology for diabetes management, about one-third of youth with T1D and LOE were not using any diabetes technology. Diabetes technology use in this group was associated with lower HbA1c. Further work should be done to increase diabetes technology use in youth with T1D and LOE.

title: Case Report: Case series: growth hormone replacement for severe growth hormone deficiency during BRAF inhibitor therapy in pediatric low-grade glioma: long-term follow-up.
abstract: Pediatric low-grade gliomas (pLGGs) involving the hypothalamic-pituitary region frequently result in endocrine dysfunction, particularly growth hormone deficiency (GHD), due to tumor location and treatment-related effects. Growth hormone replacement therapy (GHRT) is generally considered after a period of disease stability, whereas its use during active oncologic therapy remains controversial, including during BRAF inhibitor (BRAFi) treatment. We describe two pediatric patients with severe GHD who received GHRT during ongoing vemurafenib, a BRAFi, for progressive chiasmatic-hypothalamic pLGG. The first patient, a girl diagnosed in infancy with desmoplastic infantile ganglioglioma, developed severe GHD after biopsy, chemotherapy, partial tumor debulking, and targeted therapy, together with multiple additional endocrine deficiencies. The second patient, a boy with pilocytic astrocytoma, was diagnosed with severe GHD after multimodal treatment, including partial and subtotal surgical resections, chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and targeted therapy. In both cases, low-dose GHRT was initiated after multidisciplinary assessment, documented radiological stability before GHRT initiation, and family counseling regarding the absence of direct safety data during active BRAFi therapy. Treatment was titrated over two months, with regular IGF-1 monitoring and close endocrine and oncologic surveillance. During approximately six years of concomitant GHRT and vemurafenib exposure, growth stabilized and lipid parameters improved, whereas catch-up growth remained limited and bone outcomes were complex, with increased bone mineral content but persistent or worsening lumbar DXA-derived impairment. No tumor progression or secondary malignancies were detected during the reported follow-up. These two cases add to the limited evidence on GHRT administration during BRAFi therapy by documenting prolonged concomitant GHRT and vemurafenib exposure in children with severe confirmed GHD and previously progressive chiasmatic-hypothalamic pLGG. However, the limited sample size and observational nature of this report preclude conclusions about safety or efficacy. Larger prospective studies are needed to define which patients may benefit and under which monitoring conditions GHRT could be considered during BRAFi therapy.

title: Maternal gestational weight gain and offspring vitamin D level: a multicentre retrospective cohort study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study examined the association between maternal gestational weight gain (GWG) and offspring vitamin D levels.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, 0-5-year-old children attending routine health checks at 12 centres across 10 cities in Jiangsu Province (April 2014-March 2015) were enrolled via stratified random cluster sampling. Serum 25(OH)D was measured by ELISA.
RESULTS: Among 1,984 mother-offspring pairs, GWG ≤10 kg was associated with an increased risk of vitamin D deficiency (<50 nmol/L) in the unadjusted model (OR = 1.550, 95% CI: 1.196-2.008), and this association remained significant in Model 1 (OR = 1.820, 95% CI: 1.357-2.441), Model 2 (OR = 1.545, 95% CI: 1.060-2.253), and Model 3 (OR = 1.882, 95% CI: 1.228-2.883). For vitamin D insufficiency (50-<75 nmol/L), GWG >19 kg was associated with an increased risk in the unadjusted model (OR = 1.309, 95% CI: 1.026-1.670) and in Model 1 (OR = 1.312, 95% CI: 1.021-1.685), Model 2 (OR = 1.872, 95% CI: 1.305-2.684), and Model 3 (OR = 1.609, 95% CI: 1.054-2.456). This association was statistically significant in Model 3 but was no longer significant after FDR correction.
CONCLUSION: To our knowledge, this is the first multicentre study to report an association between GWG ≤10 kg and an increased risk of vitamin D deficiency in offspring, and between GWG >19 kg and an increased risk of vitamin D insufficiency. However, the latter association did not remain significant after FDR correction in sensitivity analyses based on Model 3 and requires confirmation in further studies.

Case Report: Hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia and arterial aneurysms in KAT6B-related disorder: case observation and literature perspective.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: KAT6B-related disorders (KAT6B-RD) are rare autosomal dominant chromatinopathies characterized by variable multisystem involvement and marked phenotypic heterogeneity.
CASE PRESENTATION: We describe a preterm male infant with intrauterine growth restriction who developed recurrent hypoglycemia toward the end of the first week of life during parenteral nutrition weaning, requiring a glucose infusion rate of up to 12 mg/kg/min. Biochemical findings were consistent with hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia, and glycemic control was rapidly achieved with diazoxide (initiated at 5 mg/kg/day and increased to 6.9 mg/kg/day). After treatment discontinuation at 4 months of age, he exhibited recurrent hypoglycemia again, requiring the resumption of diazoxide. The patient also exhibited complete scrotal agenesis with complex genital anomalies, agenesis of the corpus callosum, generalized hypotonia, severe feeding difficulties requiring gastrostomy, primary hypothyroidism, and aneurysmal dilation of the ascending aorta and proximal right coronary artery. Clinical exome sequencing identified a de novo heterozygous pathogenic KAT6B variant (c.3995del; p.Pro1332Leufs*2) in exon 17. Diazoxide was successfully discontinued at 12 months of age under continuous glucose monitoring.
CONCLUSION: This case highlights congenital hyperinsulinism and arterial aneurysms as a clinical association observed in a patient with KAT6B-RD. Rather than representing definitive novel features of the syndrome, these manifestations should be interpreted with caution as hypothesis-generating findings potentially linked to KAT6B-mediated epigenetic dysregulation, while accounting for potential perinatal confounding factors. These findings nonetheless support careful endocrine and cardiovascular surveillance and follow-up in patients with KAT6B-RD.

title: Hydroxyurea treatment is not significantly associated with reduced spermatogonial numbers in patients with sickle cell disease.
abstract: Hydroxyurea (HU) is considered a first-line therapy for patients with sickle cell disease (SCD). In cases of inadequate response to HU therapy, patients may receive conditioning therapy prior to haematopoietic stem cell transplantation, which can lead to depletion of the number of spermatogonia. Therefore, in pre-pubertal boys, fertility is preserved through cryopreservation of testicular tissue, although this is an experimental method. Analysis of this tissue showed a considerable loss of spermatogonia, leading to the hypothesis that HU therapy may reduce the spermatogonial number. However, evidence remains limited and conflicting. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the relationship between HU exposure and the spermatogonial number in boys with SCD. The number of spermatogonia per round seminiferous tubule (S/T) and the percentage of tubules containing spermatogonia were determined in cryopreserved testicular tissue from 27 HU-treated patients with SCD. Linear regression analyses were performed to assess their association with HU exposure. Spermatogonia were present in most boys with SCD, although in severely reduced numbers. S/T Z-scores and the percentage of tubules containing spermatogonia were not significantly associated with age at HU initiation, duration of HU exposure, or HU dose. In conclusion, in this cohort, no statistically significant association was observed between HU treatment and reduced spermatogonial numbers in patients with SCD.

title: The fixed cortical fraction assumption in Hip Structure Analysis produces systematic, sex- and age- dependent errors in femoral neck morphology estimates.
abstract: Hip Structure Analysis (HSA) estimates femoral neck morphology from dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) images using simplifying assumptions, including that cortical bone accounts for a fixed 60% of total bone mineral content at the narrow neck (cortical fraction, fc  = 0.6). The empirical basis of this assumption is poorly established, and its effect on HSA-derived structural parameters has not been systematically evaluated. PseudoDXA images were generated by direct projection of nanoCT volumes from cadaveric proximal femurs from 32 White female (ages 24-89+ years) and 30 White male (ages 18-89 years) donors. Cortical and trabecular bone were segmented separately, enabling direct measurement of fc and comparison of HSA estimates using fixed versus measured fc against nanoCT-derived reference values. Measured fc ranged from 0.23 to 0.67 and averaged 0.48 for females and 0.42 for males, both substantially below 0.6. In females, fc increased significantly with age; in males, fc decreased significantly with body weight. Using fixed fc produced large, systematic errors in HSA-derived cortical area and buckling ratio that were sex- and age-specific, reaching up to 36% for cortical area in younger individuals. Replacing fixed fc with measured fc significantly reduced errors for cortical area in both sexes and for buckling ratio in males, with significantly greater improvement in concordance for cortical area and inner radius in males. Buckling ratio errors remained large in females even with measured fc , consistent with an additional departure from the uniform cortical thickness assumption, which is hypothesized to be more pronounced in females due to the disproportionately thick inferior cortex. These findings demonstrate that the fixed fc assumption introduces systematic, sex- and age-specific errors into HSA-derived structural estimates, and that development of DXA-derived individualized fc estimation represents a meaningful step toward improving the clinical reliability of HSA for fracture risk assessment.
